capabilities.name: chart.setType
capabilities.summary: Change how price is drawn on one chart.

capabilities.name: chart.setTimeframe
capabilities.summary: Change one chart's timeframe.
capabilities.hints: 1/5/15/30/60 min, D, W, M; next/previous: one rung.

capabilities.name: chart.setSymbol
capabilities.summary: Show a different ticker on one chart. Widgets linked to the same color group follow, exactly as a manual symbol search does.

capabilities.name: chart.setSession
capabilities.summary: Show or hide pre/post-market (extended hours) on one chart.

capabilities.name: chart.setScale
capabilities.summary: Set one chart's price scale: linear (arithmetic), logarithmic, or percent.

capabilities.name: chart.applyTheme
capabilities.summary: Apply one of UCT's built-in chart color themes (canvas, candles, grid, text) to one chart.

capabilities.name: chart.setBackground
capabilities.summary: Set one chart's background to a single solid color.
capabilities.hints: Pass a hex color like #f3efe4; translate plain color names to hex.

capabilities.name: chart.setCandleColors
capabilities.summary: Set one chart's up and/or down candle colors.
capabilities.hints: Hex colors; pass null for a side that should not change.

capabilities.name: volume.setState
capabilities.summary: Show, hide, or remove one chart's built-in Volume pane.
capabilities.hints: "hide volume" is hidden (stays in the legend); "remove volume" is removed (off the chart).

capabilities.name: chart.setSetting
capabilities.summary: Change one chart display setting from UCT's approved list (grid, crosshair, scale text, legend, watermark, labels, event/IPO markers, dark-pool levels, swing labels, prev-day lines, countdown, title, color mode, thin bars, inverted scale, gradient background, Volume pane look, Heikin Ashi, Chart IQ, position calculator, Info row / Bar info fields).
capabilities.hints: value = true/false for on/off settings (crosshair.mode, header.legendMode and bgMode too); a hex color (#2962ff) for colors; a number in range. Allowed — crosshair.mode, header.legendMode: always|hold|off; textSize: 8|10|11|12|14|16|18|20|22|24|28|32|40; header.titleMode: ticker|company|both; candleColorMode: onecolor|netchange|openclose; swingLabels.sensitivity: low|medium|high; crosshair.width, prevDayLevels.high|low|close.width, volume.maLineWidth: 1|2|3|4; crosshair.style, prevDayLevels.high|low|close.style, volume.maLineStyle: solid|dashed|dotted; watermark.sizeScale: 0.5|0.75|1|1.25|1.5|2|2.5|3|4; watermark.weight: 300|400|500|600|700|800; bgMode: solid|gradient; volume.barStyle: columns|histogram; volume.paneHeightPct: 8–45 (whole); volume.maPeriod: 0–500 (whole); watermark.opacity|x|y: 0–1; positionCalc.accountSize: 0–1000000000; positionCalc.riskPct: 0–100. header.fields|barInfo: +/-field ("+Market Cap"). Anything else: no op — say where it lives in Chart Settings.
capabilities.shape: args {"setting": <one id from the list>, "value": …} — "turn the gradient off" = {"setting":"bgMode","value":"solid"}, "gradient on" = {"setting":"bgMode","value":"gradient"}, "hide the grid" = {"setting":"grid.visible","value":false}. Never invent a setting id (no "bgGradient.enabled", no "background.gradient"): an on/off wish for a setting not listed is unsupported.

capabilities.name: chart.applyTemplate
capabilities.summary: Apply one of the member's saved chart templates to ONE chart, exactly as clicking it does (Chart Settings → Templates, or right-click → Chart template): the chart takes the template's whole saved setup, its indicators included.
capabilities.hints: template = a name from chartTemplates, exactly. For several charts ("all my charts"), one op per chart.

capabilities.name: chart.resetDefaults
capabilities.summary: Restore ONE chart's look to UCT's defaults (Chart Settings → Restore defaults): colours, markers, header, watermark and display settings. The chart's indicators are kept exactly as they are.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart. Always shown as a proposal first.

capabilities.name: chart.goToDate
capabilities.summary: Scroll ONE chart so a past date is at its right edge — exactly the Time Navigator date box. A view change only: every bar stays on the chart (it is not a replay), nothing is saved; Undo scrolls back.
capabilities.hints: date = YYYY-MM-DD. "As it looked on <date>" = this (say in the reply that later bars are still there, just scrolled off to the right).

capabilities.name: chart.replay
capabilities.summary: Replay Mode (Tools → Replay): hide every bar after a date on the linked charts, as if it were that day — or exit replay (date null). A view only: nothing is saved; Undo clears it (or restores the previous cutoff).
capabilities.hints: date = YYYY-MM-DD (or the member's date word: "last friday", "oct 15") for the cutoff; null = exit replay. "As of <date>" / "replay from <date>" / "go back to <date> and hide what came after" = this; "scroll to <date>" with every bar kept = chart.goToDate.
capabilities.shape: {"date":"YYYY-MM-DD"} to replay from a date; {"date":null} to EXIT replay ("exit replay", "leave replay", "replay off", "show every bar again") — the JSON null, never the word "null" and never an "exit" or "enabled" key.

capabilities.name: chart.compare
capabilities.summary: Overlay other symbols on ONE chart (Tools → Compare Symbols): add tickers, remove some, or clear all comparisons.
capabilities.hints: add = tickers to overlay, uppercase ([] for none); remove = tickers to take off ([] for none); clear = true to remove every comparison. "Compare NVDA against QQQ on this chart" = target the NVDA chart, add [QQQ].

capabilities.name: chart.addCustomTimeframe
capabilities.summary: Add a custom timeframe (e.g. 45 minutes, 2 hours, 3 days) to ONE chart's timeframe menu, exactly like the menu's Custom interval, and optionally switch the chart to it.
capabilities.hints: unit = minutes | hours | days | weeks | months; count = how many (45 for 45 minutes); switch = true to show the chart on it now (the usual case), false to only add it to the menu.

capabilities.name: widget.add
capabilities.summary: Add ONE widget of a given type to the Charts workspace, placed automatically in empty space. Use one op per widget.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the workspace entry. "as" NAMES THE NEW WIDGET: if any later op in this plan changes the new widget (a new chart's symbol, timeframe, …), set "as" to a short unique name (new1, new2, …) and use exactly that name as those ops' target — a later op may not target a new widget whose "as" is null. Otherwise "as" is null. Example: "add 2 charts on SPY and QQQ" → widget.add{type:chart, as:"new1"}, widget.add{type:chart, as:"new2"}, chart.setSymbol@new1{SPY}, chart.setSymbol@new2{QQQ}. Never drop a ticker the member named ("open a QQQ chart" needs its chart.setSymbol). Types: chart (Chart), watchlist (Watchlist), themes (Theme Tracker), scanner (Scanner), fundamentals (Fundamentals), breadth (Breadth), aisearch (AI Search), news (News & Catalysts), notebook (Notebook), profile (Stock Profile), alerts (Alerts), calendar (UCT Terminal), optionsflow (Options Flow), nhnl (New Highs / Lows), nhnlPulse (H/L Pulse), volumescan (Volume Surge), scatter (Market Map).

capabilities.name: widget.addCharts
capabilities.summary: Add one NEW chart per symbol of an ordered list (tickers, a screen's results, or a saved watchlist), placed together in empty space. Existing widgets are never changed.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the workspace entry. symbols = the tickers, uppercase, OR {from, top} to chart a source's stocks in its order: from = the ref of a saved watchlist (its stocks, read fresh in its saved order when they apply), the "as" of a screener.run / screener.runSaved op in this request, or "lastScreen" for the last screen run here; top = how many charts (required, at most 12). timeframe: 1|5|15|30|60 minutes, D, W, M, or null to keep the default. chart_type: candles|hollow|bars|hlc|line|area or null. exact: true only if they insist on exactly that many (else fewer results just make fewer charts). Use this — not widget.add + chart.setSymbol — whenever the charts' symbols come from a screen or watchlist. Never type tickers you have not been given.
capabilities.shape: {"symbols":["NVDA"],"timeframe":"D","chart_type":null,"exact":null} or {"symbols":{"from":"<watchlist ref or screen as>","top":2},"timeframe":null,"chart_type":null,"exact":null}; timeframe 1|5|15|30|60|D|W|M (D daily, W weekly, M monthly, 60 hourly). No other keys: indicators, a row or a position cannot be set here — plan the charts alone and say in `reply` that indicators can be added next. ⛔ With NO chart in <workspace_context>, "add / open / show a <timeframe> chart of <symbol>" is THIS op on the workspace entry — never chart.setSymbol / chart.setTimeframe on a chart that does not exist.

capabilities.name: layout.current
capabilities.summary: Tell the member which named layout is open. UCT answers from the real state — use this (disposition apply) for "which layout am I on?" instead of answering yourself.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry.

capabilities.name: layout.list
capabilities.summary: List the member's named layouts. UCT answers from the real list — use this (disposition apply) whenever they ask what layouts they have, instead of listing them yourself.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry.

capabilities.name: layout.open
capabilities.summary: Open (switch to) one of the member's named layouts on the Charts workspace — exactly like clicking it in the Layout Dock.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of one entry in its `layouts` list, or the member's own words for it ("my trading layout" → "trading") — UCT matches the words itself: one match opens, several are asked about with the real names. Do not ask yourself. Only the open layout's widgets are in workspace_context; after a switch, ask again for changes on the new board.

capabilities.name: layout.saveAs
capabilities.summary: Save the current Charts workspace as a NEW named layout (it becomes the open layout). Never replaces an existing layout.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; name = the exact name the member gave. If that name is already in the layouts list, do not use this — tell the member instead. ONLY for saving the WORKSPACE/LAYOUT/BOARD: while an indicator draft is active (indicatorDrafts), "save it as X" means the indicator (indicator.saveDraft) unless the member says layout/workspace/board; if you cannot tell, ask.

capabilities.name: layout.saveCurrent
capabilities.summary: Save the board as it is now into the layout that is OPEN (only the member’s own layout). Replaces that layout’s saved copy; no Undo.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry. Use for "save these changes to my layout". For a NEW layout use layout.saveAs.

capabilities.name: layout.rename
capabilities.summary: Rename one of the member's OWN layouts (not prebuilt or built-in ones).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of the layout to rename (the open one if they say "this layout"); name = the new name exactly as given. "rename <X> to <Y>" where X is a layout name = this op, never chart.renameTab (a chart widget's TAB, only when they say "tab"). A protected layout is refused by UCT itself: plan the op, never say you can't rename.

capabilities.name: layout.create
capabilities.summary: Create a NEW, EMPTY named layout (no widgets) for the member. The current board is not touched and the new layout is NOT opened.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; name = the exact name the member gave. To save the board AS IT IS NOW, use layout.saveAs instead. If they also want to switch to it, create it now and say in the reply that they can then say "open <name>" (switching is a separate step).

capabilities.name: layout.delete
capabilities.summary: Delete one of the member's OWN saved layouts (permanent). Not the layout that is open now, not prebuilt or built-in layouts.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of that layout in the layouts list. If more than one layout could be meant, or none matches exactly, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?".

capabilities.name: layout.duplicate
capabilities.summary: Make a copy of a saved layout (its stored version) under a new name, as one of the member's own layouts. Does not open it.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of the layout to copy (the open one for "this layout"); name = the new name as given, or null when they give none (UCT names it "<name> copy" and the proposal shows it — do not ask for a name). To save the board AS IT IS NOW under a new name, use layout.saveAs instead.

capabilities.name: layout.pinToBar
capabilities.summary: Pin one of the member's layouts to the layout bar along the bottom of Charts (the library's "add to bar"). The slot goes on the end. Does NOT open the layout and does not change the board.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layoutDock entry; layout = the layout's id from the layouts list, or the member's own words for it (UCT matches them; several matches are asked about). To also switch to it, that is layout.open, a separate step.

capabilities.name: layout.unpinFromBar
capabilities.summary: Take one layout off the layout bar along the bottom of Charts (the slot menu's "Close"). The layout stays in the library: this NEVER deletes a layout (that is layout.delete).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layoutDock entry; layout = the layout's id, or the member's words for it. If they did not name one, or it sits on the bar twice, clarify with the real names.

capabilities.name: layout.moveOnBar
capabilities.summary: Reorder the layout bar along the bottom of Charts: move one layout left or right one spot (the slot menu's Move left / Move right), to the first or last spot, or to a numbered spot.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layoutDock entry; layout = the layout's id, or the member's words for it; to = "left" or "right" (one spot), "first" or "last", or a spot number counted from 1 on the left (the `spot` in the bar list).

capabilities.name: watchlist.list
capabilities.summary: List the member's saved watchlists (names and sizes). UCT answers from the real lists — use this (disposition apply) whenever they ask what watchlists they have.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlistLibrary entry.

capabilities.name: watchlist.show
capabilities.summary: Say which symbols are in one of the member's watchlists. UCT answers from the real list — use this (disposition apply) for "what's in <list>?".
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of that watchlist. "my watchlist" = the list a widget shows (shownInWidget); "the one I just made" = the list marked recent. as: name this list's STOCKS (e.g. "list1") when a later op in the same request uses them (e.g. widget.addCharts symbols {from:"list1", top:N}); else null.

capabilities.name: watchlist.add
capabilities.summary: Add tickers to one of the member's saved watchlists (the list itself, not a widget). Symbols already in the list are skipped.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist (or the "as" name of a list created earlier in this request); "my watchlist" = the list a widget shows (shownInWidget); "the one I just made" = the list marked recent. symbols = the tickers, uppercase, OR {from, top} to add a SCREEN's stocks: from = the "as" of a screener op earlier in this request (or "lastScreen" for the last screen run here), top = how many of its results, in its order (null = ALL of them — the default when they say "all" or give no number; at most 1000). Never type tickers you have not been given. If they say "my watchlist" and it is not clear which list, clarify with the real list names. One op per list.

capabilities.name: watchlist.remove
capabilities.summary: Remove specific tickers from one of the member's saved watchlists, one or several at once. Undo puts them back with their notes and order.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; "my watchlist" = the list a widget shows (shownInWidget); "the one I just made" = the list marked recent. symbols = exactly the tickers to remove ("the top three" = the first rows of the listViews entry showing it, or of its symbols when no widget shows it). For "everything except these" use watchlist.keepOnly.

capabilities.name: watchlist.keepOnly
capabilities.summary: Remove everything from one of the member's saved watchlists EXCEPT the tickers named ("keep only these", "everything except these"). One change, always shown as a proposal naming what goes; Undo puts them back with their notes and order.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; "my watchlist" = the list a widget shows (shownInWidget); "the one I just made" = the list marked recent. symbols = the tickers to KEEP ("keep the top three" = the first rows of the listViews entry showing it, or of its symbols). Every one must be in the list: a name that is not stops the whole change.

capabilities.name: watchlist.clear
capabilities.summary: Remove EVERY symbol from one of the member's saved watchlists (the list itself stays). Always shown as a proposal with the count first.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist. For only some symbols use watchlist.remove. If it is not clear which list, clarify with the real names.

capabilities.name: watchlist.delete
capabilities.summary: Delete one of the member's saved watchlists entirely (permanent). Not a list a Watchlist widget on this board is showing.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist. If more than one list could be meant, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?". To empty a list but keep it, use watchlist.clear.

capabilities.name: watchlist.create
capabilities.summary: Create a NEW saved watchlist (a named list of tickers) — only when they ask to create or make a list. "Add a watchlist" with no list name means a Watchlist WIDGET on the board: that is widget.add, not this.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlistLibrary entry; name = exactly as given. To COPY a list ("duplicate my X watchlist"), create "<X> copy" (or the name they give — do not ask for one) and add {from: the ref of X, top: null} to it. To fill it in the same request set "as" to a short name (new1) and target watchlist.add at that name; otherwise "as" is null. No name given: pick a short descriptive one (e.g. Software Over $10) not already in the watchlists list — do not ask. Never use this for a name already in the watchlists list — if they ask to put stocks in a list "called X" and X already exists, clarify (add to the existing X, or a new name); never silently append.

capabilities.name: watchlist.rename
capabilities.summary: Rename one of the member's saved watchlists.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; name = the new name exactly as given.

capabilities.name: watchlist.reorder
capabilities.summary: Reorder one of the member's saved watchlists (the saved order, permanently): sort it alphabetically (A–Z or Z–A) and/or move some tickers to the top, in the order given. Nothing is added or removed. Undo puts the old order back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; sort = az | za | null (keep the order); top = tickers to put first, in this order ([] for none). "Sort my Momentum list" = az. This rewrites the saved order. To order what a widget shows by price, change or other data, use watchlist.sortColumn.

capabilities.name: watchlist.setNote
capabilities.summary: Write, change or clear the NOTE on one ticker in one of the member's saved watchlists (the note column on the Watchlists page). Undo puts the old note back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; symbol = the ticker (it must be in that list); note = the text exactly as the member gave it ("" clears it; at most 500 characters).

capabilities.name: watchlist.sortColumn
capabilities.summary: Sort what a Watchlist or Scanner widget shows by one of its columns (price, % change, RVOL, market cap…), the header click. It changes the view, not the saved order. column null = back to the saved order. Undo puts the old sort back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the listViews entry: the one marked active for "this list", the one named as the list they name ("my Momentum list"; for "the one I just made", the watchlists entry marked recent), the only entry for "my watchlist"; several could be meant → clarify by name or position. No entry means no such widget is on this board: say so, offer watchlist.open. column = the column as they said it; direction = asc | desc | null (null = the header's own first click: Symbol A to Z, others high to low; "biggest / top / highest" = desc, "lowest / smallest" = asc). A column not showing is added. Columns: Price, Volume, % Change, Company Name, RVOL, IPO Date, Market Cap, Next Earnings, UCT Rating, $ Change, % from Open, % from High, % from Low, DCR, Dollar Volume, Sector, Industry, Theme, 5-Day, 30-Day, 60-Day, 90-Day, Attention, ATR %, ATR from 50SMA. For a permanent A to Z of the saved list use watchlist.reorder.

capabilities.name: watchlist.setColumns
capabilities.summary: Add or hide columns on a Watchlist or Scanner widget, or reset them to the defaults (the right-click column menu). Undo puts the old columns back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the listViews entry: the one marked active for "this list", the one named as the list they name ("my Momentum list"; for "the one I just made", the watchlists entry marked recent), the only entry for "my watchlist"; several could be meant → clarify by name or position. No entry means no such widget is on this board: say so, offer watchlist.open. add / hide = columns as they said them ([] for none); reset = true only for "reset my columns" (the defaults, then add / hide). Symbol and the flag star can't be hidden. Columns: Price, Volume, % Change, Company Name, RVOL, IPO Date, Market Cap, Next Earnings, UCT Rating, $ Change, % from Open, % from High, % from Low, DCR, Dollar Volume, Sector, Industry, Theme, 5-Day, 30-Day, 60-Day, 90-Day, Attention, ATR %, ATR from 50SMA. Nothing else exists: a column not listed is refused, never swapped for a near one.

capabilities.name: watchlist.arrangeColumns
capabilities.summary: Move a column on a Watchlist or Scanner widget (as dragging its header does) or set its width in pixels (as dragging its gridline does). Undo puts the old columns back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the listViews entry: the one marked active for "this list", the one named as the list they name ("my Momentum list"; for "the one I just made", the watchlists entry marked recent), the only entry for "my watchlist"; several could be meant → clarify by name or position. No entry means no such widget is on this board: say so, offer watchlist.open. column = a column that shows; before / after = another showing column (one of them, or neither); width = pixels (a column's minimum to 600), or null.

capabilities.name: watchlist.step
capabilities.summary: Move to the next or previous ticker in a Watchlist or Scanner widget, in the order it shows them (the arrow keys; the linked chart follows). Also first / last. Undo goes back to the ticker before.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the listViews entry: the one marked active for "this list", the one named as the list they name ("my Momentum list"; for "the one I just made", the watchlists entry marked recent), the only entry for "my watchlist"; several could be meant → clarify by name or position. No entry means no such widget is on this board: say so, offer watchlist.open. direction = next | previous | first | last; by = how many rows (null = 1): "next ticker" = next, "skip two" = next by 3. It wraps at the ends, as the arrow keys do. Never compute the ticker yourself.

capabilities.name: watchlist.readView
capabilities.summary: Say what a Watchlist or Scanner widget shows right now: its tickers in on-screen order (its column sort applied), its sort and columns. Use it for "what's at the top of this list". Its rows are in the listViews context too, so "remove the top three" can name them directly.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the listViews entry: the one marked active for "this list", the one named as the list they name ("my Momentum list"; for "the one I just made", the watchlists entry marked recent), the only entry for "my watchlist"; several could be meant → clarify by name or position. No entry means no such widget is on this board: say so, offer watchlist.open. as: name these STOCKS (e.g. "view1") when a later op in the same request uses them, e.g. watchlist.add symbols {from:"view1", top:3}; else null. It never reports prices.

capabilities.name: watchlist.setFlag
capabilities.summary: Flag or unflag tickers: the star on a row and Shift+F, one Flagged set across the whole app. Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the flagged entry; symbols = the tickers, uppercase; flagged = true to flag, false to unflag. Never type tickers you have not been given: "this one" is the chart's symbol, "the top three" is the first rows of the listViews entry.

capabilities.name: screener.run
capabilities.summary: Run a stock screen on UCT's Screener and show the real matches (count + top rows). Changes nothing in UCT. Use this for "show me / find stocks with …".
capabilities.hints: target = the screener entry ref. Comparisons, OR/NOT, rank: `compose`. filters: each {field: a key from `fields` (never invented), op, value, max, values}. Numbers: op gt|gte|lt|lte|eq|between, value, max (between only, else null), values null; % fields take 5 for 5%, $ fields take dollars (10M = 10000000). yes/no: op eq, value 1|0. (list) fields: op in|not_in, values = the member's own words (["software"]) — UCT matches real values; value/max null. "(latest session)" fields only when a session is named ("today", "yesterday"); "$10M a day" / "per day" if none named = the 30-day average, not share volume. A measure not in `fields`: say so, never substitute. sort_field/sort_dir or null. mode refine = change the LAST screen, else new. show: rows (null = 10, max 25). as: name the RESULT (screen1) when a later op uses its stocks ({from:"screen1", top:null} = all); else null. within: a watchlist ref only if they name that list ("in Momentum"); else null (whole market).
capabilities.shape: a refinement that only changes the ORDER ("sort them by 3-month performance") is {"filters":[],"sort_field":"chg_pct_3m","sort_dir":"desc","mode":"refine","show":null,"as":null,"within":null,"logic":null,"rank":null} — filters is ALWAYS present ([] when nothing is added), sort_field is a key from `fields`, sort_dir is exactly "asc" or "desc" (never "descending"), and there is no nested "sort" object.

capabilities.name: screener.runSaved
capabilities.summary: Run one of the member's saved screens (or a UCT starter screen) and show the real matches.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry; screen = the id of an entry in savedScreens (never invent one; clarify with the real names if unsure). show: rows (null = 10). as: name its RESULT when a later op in the same request uses its stocks; else null.

capabilities.name: screener.state
capabilities.summary: Say what the last screen run here was: its filters, sort and number of matches.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

capabilities.name: screener.listSaved
capabilities.summary: List the member's saved screens and UCT's starter screens.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

capabilities.name: alert.list
capabilities.summary: Show the member's price alerts from UCT's real alert list: which are active, which went off (and when). Use this (disposition apply) for "show my alerts", "do I have an alert on NVDA?", "which alerts went off today?".
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the alertLibrary entry. symbol: one ticker to filter by, or null. status: active | triggered | all, or null (= all). triggered_today: true only for "today"; else null. These are PRICE alerts only — indicator alerts (RSI, MACD…) are not listed here.

capabilities.name: alert.create
capabilities.summary: Create ONE price alert in UCT's Alerts: it goes off ONCE when the stock is at or above (direction above) or at or below (direction below) a price level, checked while the market is open. Only price levels — no percent-move, indicator, volume or time alerts; alerts cannot be paused, edited or made repeating.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the alertLibrary entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase; price = the level as a number; direction = above ("crosses above", "breaks above", "rises to", "gets to … from below") or below ("drops below", "falls to", "breaks down under"). If they give a level WITHOUT saying above or below (e.g. "an alert on NVDA at 200", "when it hits 200"), clarify with choices above / below — never guess. One op per alert, at most 5 in one request. An earlier alert at that level that already went off does NOT stop a new one — create it. Creating is always shown to the member as a proposal first, so plan it (disposition propose) — even inside a question ("why is TSLA moving? and set an alert above 300": propose the alert AND ask research for the question). It watches that chart's symbol with the instance's own settings, on the chart's timeframe or another native one. Undo deletes it.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the indicatorAlertLibrary entry; instance = the id of the indicator from that chart's indicators entry (never a name); chart = the ref of the chart it is on; plot = null, or for several lines the address the catalog names (macd.signal) — not sure which line: ask. condition = above | below | cross_above | cross_below | cross_zero | touch_upper | touch_lower ("crosses above 70" = cross_above; "is over 70" = above); threshold = the level, else null. The member's own yes/no signal: trigger = becomes_true ("turns on") | becomes_false ("turns off") | is_true, condition and threshold null; trigger = null otherwise. timeframe = null for the chart's own, or 1 | 5 | 15 | 30 | 60 | D | W | M ("alert on the weekly RSI" = W). capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; from = the swing start {date, price} (the low for an up move); to = the swing end {date, price}. "Fib from the Oct 7 low at 150 to the Oct 28 high at 190". a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; color = a colour name or #hex, null = the member's drawing default; style = solid | dashed | dotted, null = solid.

capabilities.name: drawing.addHorizontalRay
capabilities.summary: Draw a HORIZONTAL RAY from a date at a price, extending to the right — the toolbar's own horizontal ray (a level that starts on a day, e.g. a breakout level from its breakout date). Undo removes it.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; date = where the ray starts; price = its level; a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; color / style as for other drawings (null = defaults). A level with no start date is drawing.addLevel.

capabilities.name: drawing.addText
capabilities.summary: Place a TEXT NOTE on a chart's symbol at a date and price — the toolbar's own text tool, with the member's exact words. Undo removes it.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; text = the note exactly as the member said it (never reworded, up to 200 characters); date / price = where it sits; a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; color = a colour name or #hex, null = the member's default.

capabilities.name: drawing.addAvwap
capabilities.summary: Draw an ANCHORED VWAP on a chart's symbol starting from a date — the toolbar's own anchored VWAP (volume-weighted average price from that session forward). Undo removes it.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; date = the anchor session (a trading day: an earnings day, a low, "last friday"); price = the price on that day the member named, or the price they are looking at there (the anchor's level — the VWAP itself is computed from the bars); a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; color null = the member's default.

capabilities.name: drawing.list
capabilities.summary: List the drawings on a chart's symbol (every chart on that symbol shares them): each one's id, tool, level and style. Read-only.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol.

capabilities.name: drawing.addLevel
capabilities.summary: Draw a HORIZONTAL LINE at a price on a chart's symbol — the price axis's own "Draw horizontal line at $X". Every chart on that symbol shows it; Undo removes it. A level that starts on a date is drawing.addHorizontalRay; every other tool has its own capability or drawing.add.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; price = the level (a number, as the member said it — never invented); color = a colour name or #hex, null = the member's drawing default; style = solid | dashed | dotted, null = solid. One op per level. A level the member describes without a number ("the recent high", "support") has no price — clarify, never guess.

capabilities.name: drawing.style
capabilities.summary: Change ONE drawing's colour, line style or width (what its settings do). Undo puts the old style back.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id from that entry's drawings (the most recent one the member drew is last; the one marked recent is the one I last drew or changed); color / style / width null = leave as is. "Make that line pink and dashed" / "make it red" = the recent one (else the line just drawn).

capabilities.name: drawing.remove
capabilities.summary: Remove ONE drawing by id from a chart's symbol (every chart and layout showing it). Refused for a locked drawing and for one an alert is attached to. A hidden drawing is shown as a proposal first. Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id. "Remove the line I just added" = the newest one (or the one marked recent). To remove EVERY drawing use drawing.clear.

capabilities.name: drawing.setVisible
capabilities.summary: Show or hide ONE drawing (its eye in the drawing's menu) on a chart's symbol — every chart on that symbol. Nothing is deleted. Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id; visible = true to show, false to hide. For EVERY drawing on the symbol use drawing.setAllVisible.

capabilities.name: drawing.lock
capabilities.summary: Lock or unlock ONE drawing (its lock in the drawing's menu): a locked drawing can't be moved, restyled or removed until it is unlocked. Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id; locked = true to lock, false to unlock.

capabilities.name: drawing.setLevel
capabilities.summary: Move a HORIZONTAL line (or a horizontal ray) to a new price — what dragging it does. Refused for a locked drawing. A line an alert is attached to is shown first (its alert moves with it). Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = the horizontal line's id (the one marked recent for "move it"); price = the new level as the member said it — never invented.

capabilities.name: drawing.setAllVisible
capabilities.summary: Show or hide EVERY drawing on a chart's symbol at once (every chart on that symbol). Nothing is deleted. Undo puts each one back as it was.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; visible = true to show them all, false to hide them all.

capabilities.name: drawing.clear
capabilities.summary: Remove EVERY drawing on a chart's symbol (every chart and layout showing it) — always shown as a proposal first. Locked drawings and drawings with an alert attached are kept (and said). Undo puts them all back.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol.

capabilities.name: drawing.add
capabilities.summary: Draw any other toolbar tool from dates and prices: extended line, vertical line, circle, arrow, Fibonacci extension, pitchfork, parallel channel, cup curve, Measure, Price Range, Bars & Time or Price Move. Every chart on that symbol shows it; Undo removes it.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; points = [{date, price}, …] in the tool's order: extended: first point, second point; vertical: the date (price null); circle: one corner, opposite corner; arrow: tail, tip; fibext: move start, move end; pitchfork: pivot, left shoulder, right shoulder; channel: base start, base end, a point on the parallel line; cup: left rim, bottom, right rim; measure: start, end; priceRange: start, end; dateRange: start, end; advance: setup candle, candle where the move tops. a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; a point with no number ("the low") has no anchor — clarify, never guess. color / style null = defaults.

capabilities.name: drawing.setAnchors
capabilities.summary: Move the anchors of ONE drawing (what dragging its points does): any tool, any point, a new date and/or price. "Flatten that line" sets every point to the first point's price. Refused for a locked drawing. A drawing with an alert is shown first (its alert follows). Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id (the recent one for "it"); points = [{point, date, price}]: point 1 = the first of that drawing's `anchors`, date / price null = keep it. "Move the second point to Nov 1 at 210" = one item; a whole drawing up $5 = one item per point, from its anchors. a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented.

capabilities.name: drawing.setProps
capabilities.summary: Change settings on ONE drawing, as its right-click menu does: fill, price label, percent label, arrow size, Measure label fields and position, a note's words, font, size, bold, italic, background, border. Each tool has only its own settings; one it lacks is refused and its real ones named. Colour, width and line style are drawing.style. Undo puts them back.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id; set = [{prop, value, opacity}]. prop by tool: rectangle fillColor, showPercentChange; horizontal line / ray showPriceLabel; arrow arrowSize (small | medium | large); Measure / Price Range showDollar, showPercent, showBars, showTime, labelPos (top | center | bottom); Bars & Time showBars, showTime, labelPos; Price Move showDollar, showPercent; note text, fontFamily, fontSize (8-64), bold, italic, bgEnabled, bgColor, borderEnabled, borderColor. value = true / false for a switch, a colour, null = back to default. opacity = 0-100 for a colour, null = default.

capabilities.name: drawing.setFibLevels
capabilities.summary: Edit a Fibonacci retracement or extension's Levels… menu: show or hide a level, colour a level, turn the fill between two neighbouring levels on or off and colour it, or reset them all to defaults. The anchors and any level alerts are not touched. Undo puts them back.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = the Fibonacci's id. levels = [{level, visible, color}], level as the member says it (0.786 or 78.6), visible false = "remove the 78.6"; null = leave. bands = [{from, to, enabled, color, opacity}] between two neighbouring levels, color null = its default, opacity = 0-100 or null. reset = true for "reset the fib levels" (levels and bands then both []). Levels are the tool's own table: there are no custom levels.

capabilities.name: drawing.setAlert
capabilities.summary: Set an alert that FOLLOWS a drawing (the drawing menu's "Set alert…"): a trendline, ray, extended line, horizontal line or ray, or one Fibonacci level. A sloped line's level moves with time; moving the drawing moves the alert. Always shown first; Undo removes the alert unless it already went off.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id; direction = above ("breaks above", "gets above") or below ("breaks below", "loses"). If they do not say which side, clarify — never guess. level = the Fibonacci level (0.618 or 61.8), else null. Plan it, disposition propose. For a price with no drawing use alert.create.

capabilities.name: drawing.duplicate
capabilities.summary: Duplicate ONE drawing (its menu's Duplicate): an unlocked duplicate drawing just below the original on the same symbol — every chart on that symbol shows it. The duplicate is the drawing "it" means next. Undo removes the duplicate only.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id (the one marked recent for "duplicate it"). Not offered for a hidden drawing (show it first) or a retired tool. To copy a drawing to a DIFFERENT symbol there is no capability — say so.

capabilities.name: drawing.setPositionAlerts
capabilities.summary: Set a POSITION drawing's alerts (its menu's Alerts row): entry, stop, target, or all three. Each is an alert bound to that level, going off on the side the menu gives it (stop = the losing side, target = the winning side, entry = toward the entry from the current price). Always shown first; Undo removes them unless one already went off.
capabilities.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = the position's id; levels = any of "entry", "stop", "target" ("all three" / "all its alerts" = all three). The side is the position's own — never ask the member. A line, ray or Fibonacci is drawing.setAlert.

capabilities.name: drawing.setActiveBoard
capabilities.summary: Switch the Drawing Board the member draws on (Drawing Boards in the chart toolbar). Boards are named sheets of drawings shared by EVERY chart and symbol: switching changes what every chart shows and draws on. Not a layout and not the workspace.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the drawingBoards entry; board = the board's name as the member said it (a name from its boards list, e.g. "Swing" or "Board 2"). UCT matches it itself; when the member gives no name, or it could be more than one board, clarify with the real names. Never pick one. Boards cannot be switched for one chart only.

capabilities.name: drawing.createBoard
capabilities.summary: Make a new Drawing Board and switch to it, exactly like "New board" in Drawing Boards: new drawings go on it, and the other boards keep theirs. Not a new layout or a blank workspace.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the drawingBoards entry; name = the name the member gave, or null for none (UCT shows it as "Board N", as the panel does).

capabilities.name: drawing.renameBoard
capabilities.summary: Rename one Drawing Board (the pencil on its row in Drawing Boards).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the drawingBoards entry; board = the board's current name as the member said it ("Board 2" for an unnamed one); to = the new name. When they do not say which board and there is more than one, clarify with the real names.

capabilities.name: drawing.deleteBoard
capabilities.summary: Delete one Drawing Board and every drawing on it, on every symbol (the bin on its row in Drawing Boards). Permanent: it cannot be undone. Never the last board.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the drawingBoards entry; board = the board's name exactly as the member said it. If they did not name a board ("delete my board", "delete this board"), or it could be more than one, clarify with the real names. Never pick one, and never the active board unless they named it. UCT always shows a confirmation card first, so do not ask "are you sure?".

capabilities.name: indicator.list
capabilities.summary: List the indicators on ONE chart (as its legend names them): built-in or custom, shown or hidden, on the price chart or in its own pane. UCT answers from the chart's real state — use this (disposition apply) whenever they ask what indicators are on a chart, whether one is on, or which are hidden, instead of answering yourself.
capabilities.hints: target = the indicators entry for the chart the member means (with several charts and no chart named, ask which). filter: hidden | shown | null (all).

capabilities.name: indicator.openCreate
capabilities.summary: Open the Create Indicator PANEL (the visual builder) on one chart — ONLY when the member asks for the panel by name ("open Create Indicator"), or to Modify a saved custom indicator there. Their request is typed into its box; nothing is built or saved. To BUILD an indicator with the member in this chat, use indicator.draft.
capabilities.hints: target = the indicators entry for the chart. request = the member's description of the indicator, in their words (≤ 600 characters), or null to just open it. defId = a custom indicator's defId from that chart's list (only to modify it), else null — never a name. Use ONLY for an explicit request to open the panel ("open Create Indicator", "open the indicator builder/editor") or to modify a saved custom indicator there. "Build/make/create/write me an indicator…" is indicator.draft (built right here in the chat), not this. Adding, removing, showing or hiding indicators on a chart is indicator.add/remove/show/hide.

capabilities.name: indicator.add
capabilities.summary: Add ONE indicator to ONE chart — exactly what the Indicator Library's Add to Chart does. Built-in indicators or the member's own saved ones; Undo removes it again.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. defId = an id from indicatorCatalog (never invented, never a name). The SAME indicator on several charts = one indicator.add per chart named, same defId; if it isn't clear which charts, ask. Classic overlay averages (the legacy EMA/SMA rows) and Volume Profile are NOT added this way — say they live in Chart Settings. inputs = null for the indicator's defaults, else [{key, value}] with ONLY keys from that row's `settings` ("a 20 EMA" → movingAverage, [{key:"period",value:20},{key:"maType",value:"ema"}]; "RSI 7" → rsi, [{key:"period",value:7}]). Every number or type the member named goes in inputs — never drop one or add a default instead. A setting the row does not list: say it isn't available; never guess a key. A moving average named by its LENGTH only ("the 9 and 20", "a 50 ma"): EMA for 8, 9, 10, 20 and 21, SMA for 50 and above (the member's default — say which you used); any other length: ask EMA or SMA.

capabilities.name: indicator.remove
capabilities.summary: Remove ONE indicator (its whole group, e.g. all COT panes) from ONE chart — the settings ✕ / legend Delete. Always shown as a proposal first, listing anything it would disconnect. Undo restores it exactly (same identity, reconnected inputs).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

capabilities.name: indicator.update
capabilities.summary: Change the settings of ONE indicator already on ONE chart, in place — its length, its moving-average type, or another setting its row lists (what the indicator's settings dialog does). Never adds a second copy. Undo puts the old settings back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). inputs = [{key, value}] with ONLY keys from that indicator's settings, and ONLY the settings the member named — everything else stays as it is (an EMA stays an EMA unless they name a type). "make it a 9" right after adding an EMA 20 → that EMA, [{key:"period",value:9}]; "change that to an SMA" → [{key:"maType",value:"sma"}]. Use this — never indicator.remove + indicator.add — to change an indicator that is already on the chart.

capabilities.name: indicator.show
capabilities.summary: Show ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

capabilities.name: indicator.hide
capabilities.summary: Hide ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

capabilities.name: indicator.draft
capabilities.summary: THE DEFAULT for building a custom indicator: build it WITH the member right here in this chat ("build/make me an indicator that…", "also require RSI above 50", "what would you add?") — one draft, through Create Indicator's own engine. Questions and advice change nothing. Never saves (indicator.saveDraft does).
capabilities.hints: target = the ACTIVE draft's ref to continue it (follow-ups like "also…", "make it…", "what would you add?" go to the active draft); the NEW-draft entry only when the member starts a different indicator or edits one of yourIndicators (edit = its defId, else null). With an active draft, "this indicator" / "the indicator" / "it" means that draft — do not ask which. If several drafts could be meant and none is active or named, ask which. chart = the ref of the chart the member names for it, else null (a draft keeps its own chart). message = the member's words, verbatim — never your own formula or interpretation. NEVER add indicator.previewDraft unless the member asked in this message to see/preview it.

capabilities.name: indicator.previewDraft
capabilities.summary: Show an indicator draft as this tab's ONE live preview on a chart (not saved; moves off any other chart). Only when the member asks to see it.
capabilities.hints: target = the draft's ref (usually the active one). chart = the ref of the chart to preview on — the one the member names, or the only chart; if several charts and none named, ask which. Never preview unasked.

capabilities.name: indicator.saveDraft
capabilities.summary: Save an indicator draft as one of the member's indicators (Create Indicator's own Save; a new indicator, or a new version of the one being edited) — always shown as a proposal with the builder's own summary first. addTo: charts to add the SAVED indicator to afterwards (each added separately, with its own receipt).
capabilities.hints: Use when the member saves THE INDICATOR: "save it", "save it as X", "save the indicator/draft" while an indicator draft is active (the active indicatorDrafts entry) — that "it" is the draft, NOT the workspace layout (layout.saveAs is only for an explicit layout/workspace/board). target = the draft's ref (usually the active one). name = the name the member gave ("save it as Bullish Trend" → "Bullish Trend"), else null — never a separate indicator.draft op for the name. addTo = [] UNLESS the member asked in this message to add/apply/put it on a chart; then only the charts' refs from the charts section that they named. Saving and adding to a chart are separate intents. "Save the indicator" with one active draft is that draft — do not ask which.

capabilities.name: indicator.undoDraft
capabilities.summary: Undo the last change in an indicator draft, exactly, when there is nothing of mine to Undo (e.g. after a reload). Never touches a chart or a saved indicator.
capabilities.hints: target = the draft's ref. Only for "undo the last change to my draft" when the normal Undo has nothing.

capabilities.name: indicator.discardDraft
capabilities.summary: Throw away ONE unsaved indicator draft ("never mind that indicator", "discard the draft"). Always shown as a proposal first. Saved indicators and charts are never touched.
capabilities.hints: target = the draft's ref (usually the active one). Only a draft — to remove an indicator from a chart use indicator.remove.

capabilities.name: chartSetup.copyLook
capabilities.summary: Make ONE chart look like another chart on the board: it takes the other chart's colours, theme, chart type, scale and display settings. Its own indicators, comparisons and timeframe menu stay exactly as they are. Shown as a proposal first; Undo puts the old look back.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart that CHANGES; from = the ref of the chart to copy the look FROM. "Make the left chart look like the right one" → target = left, from = right.

capabilities.name: chartSetup.removeTimeframe
capabilities.summary: Remove a CUSTOM timeframe (e.g. 45 minutes, 2 hours) from ONE chart's timeframe menu — the menu's own ✕. Built-in timeframes cannot be removed. Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: timeframe = the custom code as the chart lists it (e.g. "45", "2h", "3D") or words ("45m", "2 hours").

capabilities.name: chartSetup.favoriteTimeframe
capabilities.summary: Star or un-star a timeframe on ONE chart (the timeframe menu's ★): starred timeframes show in the chart's header bar. Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: timeframe = a code (1, 5, 15, 30, 60, D, W, M, or a custom one the chart has); favorite = true to star, false to un-star.

capabilities.name: chartSetup.compareDisplay
capabilities.summary: Change how ONE chart's comparison overlays are shown (Tools → Compare Symbols): each overlay's scale ("same" = share the main price scale, "new" = its own % scale), showing or hiding an overlay, and "Group only" (hide the chart's own symbol). To add or remove overlays use chart.compare.
capabilities.hints: symbols = the compared tickers this applies to ([] = every comparison on the chart); scale = same | new | null (keep); visible = true | false | null (keep); groupOnly = true | false | null (keep).

capabilities.name: chartSetup.setRange
capabilities.summary: Show ONE chart over a set date range: the range bar's buttons (3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y, 5Y, Origin; Origin = from the first bar). A view change: every bar stays on the chart, nothing is drawn or removed, and the chart keeps this window on the next ticker until it is panned or reset. Undo puts the previous view back.
capabilities.hints: range = one of 3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y, 5Y, Origin. "One year" = 1Y, "year to date" = YTD, "five years" = 5Y, "since IPO" = Origin. Other spans have no button: use chart.goToDate, or say which ranges exist.

capabilities.name: chartSetup.resetView
capabilities.summary: Reset ONE chart's view (right-click → Reset view): the default window with the newest bar in place, and the price scale back on auto. A view change: settings, drawings and indicators are untouched. No Undo.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart. For a chart's SETTINGS use chart.resetDefaults.

capabilities.name: chartSetup.openSettings
capabilities.summary: Open ONE chart's own Chart Settings dialog for the member (the gear on the chart's header, right-click → Chart settings, Alt+,), so they can look or edit there themselves. Changes no setting; no Undo needed.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart. Only when they ask to OPEN / SHOW / BRING UP the chart's settings; to CHANGE a setting use chart.setSetting. "Open settings" alone (no chart) is the Settings page (app.open).

capabilities.name: chartSetup.stepBars
capabilities.summary: Step ONE chart's view back (older bars) or forward (newer bars) by whole bars: the Time Navigator's ◀ / ▶ buttons, one bar per click, up to 100 bars at once. A view change: nothing is drawn, removed or saved. Undo puts the previous view back.
capabilities.hints: direction = back | forward; bars = how many bars, 1 to 100 ("a bar" = 1). For a date use chart.goToDate; for a span, chartSetup.setRange. Not Replay Mode's cutoff (chart.replay).

capabilities.name: chartSetup.zoom
capabilities.summary: Zoom ONE chart's time axis in (fewer, wider bars) or out (more, narrower bars), like pressing + or - on the chart, 1 to 10 presses at once. A view change: nothing is drawn, removed or saved. Undo puts the previous view back.
capabilities.hints: direction = in | out; steps = key presses, 1 to 10 (1 when they don't say; "a lot" = 3). For a named span (3M, 1Y…) use chartSetup.setRange; "zoom out to weekly / monthly bars" is a timeframe (chart.setTimeframe); the price axis is chartSetup.autoScale.

capabilities.name: chartSetup.autoScale
capabilities.summary: Put ONE chart's price scale back on auto-scale so it fits the bars again (the price axis menu → Auto-scale; double-clicking the price numbers does the same), after the scale was dragged or squeezed by hand. Only the price scale: the time window, settings, drawings and indicators are untouched. No Undo.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart. Log / percent / arithmetic is chart.setScale; to also reset the time window use chartSetup.resetView.

capabilities.name: chartSetup.setIndicatorsHidden
capabilities.summary: Hide or bring back EVERYTHING drawn over the candles on ONE chart at once (Alt+Shift+I): every indicator, every moving average and Volume. Temporary: a reload brings them back, nothing is removed or saved. To hide just the moving averages use chartSetup.setMovingAverages; for one indicator, indicator.hide.
capabilities.hints: hidden = true to hide them all, false to bring them back.

capabilities.name: chartSetup.setMovingAverages
capabilities.summary: Hide or show EVERY moving average on ONE chart at once (Ctrl+M). They stay on the chart, hidden, and this is saved. Other indicators are untouched. Undo puts each one back as it was.
capabilities.hints: visible = false to hide them all, true to show them all.

capabilities.name: chartSetup.saveTemplate
capabilities.summary: Save ONE chart's current settings as one of the member's chart templates (Chart Settings → Templates → Save as Template) — its look and its indicators, exactly what the button saves. A template with the same name is replaced (then it is shown first). Undo puts the old list back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the chartTemplateLibrary entry; chart = the ref of the chart to save from; name = exactly as the member said it (at most 40 characters).

capabilities.name: chartSetup.deleteTemplate
capabilities.summary: Delete one of the member's saved chart templates (a template's ✕ in Chart Settings → Templates). Charts that used it keep their settings. Shown first; Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the chartTemplateLibrary entry; name = a template name from that entry, exactly.

capabilities.name: chartSetup.compareGroup
capabilities.summary: Compare ONE chart against a whole GROUP (Tools → Compare Symbols → Themes / Sectors / Industries): add every member of a theme, sector or industry as overlay lines, remove a compared group, or put a compared group on the main price scale ("same") or its own % scale ("new"). For single tickers use chart.compare.
capabilities.hints: action = add | remove | scale. group = the group's name as the member said it ("semis", "AI Chips", "Technology"); UCT matches it itself and asks when it could be more than one, so pass the words, never a guess. groupType = theme | sector | industry when the member said which, else any. scale = same | new for action scale, else null. "Compare NVDA against the semis group" = target the NVDA chart, action add, group "semis".

capabilities.name: chartMenu.askAi
capabilities.summary: Open Ask AI about ONE chart's stock, as its right-click "Ask AI about {symbol}" does (Research, AI section). Leaves Charts; changes nothing; no Undo.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart. Only when they ask to OPEN Ask AI about it; answer data questions here.

capabilities.name: chartMenu.resetWatermark
capabilities.summary: Put ONE chart's dragged watermark back in the centre (Chart Settings → Watermark → "Reset to center"). Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart. A set position, size or hiding is chart.setSetting.

capabilities.name: drawing.positionCalculator
capabilities.summary: Open the Position Calculator on ONE chart (the drawing toolbar's Position tool) with an entry, a stop and a target price: its panel sizes the trade from the account size and risk % saved there, and the chart shows the three price lines. Long or short comes from the stop being below or above the entry. A view: nothing is saved. Undo puts the calculator back as it was.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart. entry, stop, target = the member's prices; a price they did not give is null (then ask — never guess one, never use the current price). side = "long" / "short" only when they said it, else null (it is read from entry vs stop). The old 3-point position DRAWING is retired: this is the only way to place a position.

capabilities.name: drawing.saveDefaults
capabilities.summary: Make ONE drawing's style the default for new drawings on ONE chart (the drawing menu's "Save as default"): its colour, width, line style, text size and that tool's own settings become the chart's drawing defaults. Drawings already on the chart do not change. Undo puts the previous defaults back.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart the member means (the one showing the drawing); drawing = the id from that symbol's drawings entry (the recent one for "this line"). To restyle a drawing itself use drawing.style; to change the defaults by name use chart.setSetting.

capabilities.name: drawing.favoriteTool
capabilities.summary: Star or unstar a DRAWING TOOL as a favourite (the ★ in the drawing toolbar's tools menu): starred tools sit on the floating favourites bar on every chart in this browser. Undo puts the favourites back.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart whose toolbar they mean (the selected one; the list is the same on every chart); tool = the toolbar tool's id; favorite = true to star, false to unstar. Only for a drawing TOOL — flagging or starring a ticker is the watchlist's flag (watchlist.setFlag), never this.

capabilities.name: indicatorStyle.set
capabilities.summary: Change how ONE indicator on ONE chart looks — its colour (or a histogram's up / down colours), line width, line style, plot style, dot size (on an indicator that draws dots), or which chart timeframes it shows on — exactly what its settings / Inspector offer. One change per op; Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry; instance = the indicator's id from that chart's indicators list (or "#20" for the one of length 20, "#20:ema"). property = color | upColor | downColor | lineWidth (1–4, or "thicker" / "thinner") | lineStyle (solid | dashed | dotted) | plotStyle (line, histogram, area… as offered) | overlap | showOn (which chart timeframes it draws on: value = "daily", "weekly", "daily and weekly", "intraday", "daily and above" or "all" — "only show it on the daily" = showOn daily) | dotSize (small | medium | large — "medium" is the default; only an indicator that draws dots, e.g. "make the RS dots large" = dotSize large). value = the member's value (a colour name or #hex for colours). output = which line, colour or dot output when the indicator has several (its label), else null. "Make the 9 green and the 20 red and dashed" = three ops.

capabilities.name: indicatorStyle.placeIn
capabilities.summary: Move ONE indicator on ONE chart to where it draws — on the price pane, on the volume pane, in its own pane, inside another indicator's pane, or back to automatic (the Inspector's "Display in"). Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart's indicatorEdits entry; instance = the indicator; place = price | volume | pane (its own) | auto | another indicator on that chart (its id or name) to draw inside its pane.

capabilities.name: indicatorStyle.setCalcTimeframe
capabilities.summary: Calculate ONE indicator on another timeframe's bars (a weekly RSI on a daily chart), or back on the chart's own — the chart's timeframe does not change. Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart's indicatorEdits entry; instance = the indicator; timeframe = 1, 5, 15, 30, 60, D, W, M or "chart". Not showOn (which charts it shows on) and not chart.setTimeframe. "Put the RSI on weekly" is unclear: ask which.

capabilities.name: pane.move
capabilities.summary: Reorder ONE chart's panes (Chart Data → Arrange): move a pane up, down, to the top or bottom, or above / below another pane ("move RSI above price"). Undo puts the order back.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart's indicatorEdits entry; pane = price | volume | an indicator drawn in its own pane (its id, name or kind, e.g. "rsi"); to = up | down | top | bottom | above | below; relativeTo = the other pane for above / below, else null.

capabilities.name: pane.resize
capabilities.summary: Change the height of ONE pane on ONE chart (what dragging its divider does): a percent of the chart's height, bigger, smaller, or back to automatic. Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart's indicatorEdits entry; pane = price | volume | an indicator in its own pane; size = a percent (4–90) or "bigger" | "smaller" | "auto".

capabilities.name: indicatorCopy.duplicate
capabilities.summary: Add a second copy of ONE indicator on the same chart, with everything it is configured with (the legend's Duplicate). Undo removes only the copy.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart's indicatorEdits entry; instance = the indicator to copy. To put indicators on ANOTHER chart use indicatorCopy.copyTo.

capabilities.name: indicatorCopy.copyTo
capabilities.summary: Copy indicators from one chart onto ANOTHER chart, exactly as configured (colours, settings, panes and links between them — the Indicator templates copy). One op per destination chart; an indicator already there is skipped and said. Undo removes what was added.
capabilities.hints: target = the DESTINATION chart's indicatorEdits entry; from = the ref of the chart to copy FROM; instances = the indicators to copy (ids or names from that chart), or [] for all of them. "Copy these indicators to all my charts" = one op per other chart.

capabilities.name: indicatorTemplate.list
capabilities.summary: List the member's saved INDICATOR templates and the indicators in each, from the real list. Use this (disposition apply) for "what indicator templates do I have".
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the indicatorTemplateLibrary entry.

capabilities.name: indicatorTemplate.apply
capabilities.summary: Add the indicators of ONE saved INDICATOR template to ONE chart, each exactly as saved. Nothing on the chart is removed; one already there is skipped and said. Undo removes what was added. A CHART template (look and settings) is chart.applyTemplate instead.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart's indicatorEdits entry. template = a name from indicatorTemplateLibrary, exactly. Several charts = one op per chart; if it isn't clear which charts, ask. A name in both that entry and chartTemplates: ask which they mean.

capabilities.name: indicatorTemplate.save
capabilities.summary: Save the indicators on ONE chart as a named INDICATOR template (settings, colours, panes; no alerts). A template with that name is replaced only after the member approves it. Undo puts the list back. A chart's whole look is chartSetup.saveTemplate instead.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the indicatorTemplateLibrary entry; chart = the ref of the chart to save from; name = exactly as the member said it (at most 40 characters). It saves every indicator on that chart.

capabilities.name: indicatorTemplate.delete
capabilities.summary: Delete one of the member's saved INDICATOR templates. Indicators already on charts stay. Shown first; Undo puts it back. A chart template is chartSetup.deleteTemplate instead.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the indicatorTemplateLibrary entry; name = a name from that entry, exactly.

capabilities.name: definition.search
capabilities.summary: Find indicators by name or what they do — UCT's built-in indicators and the member's own saved ones (never anyone else's). Read-only.
capabilities.hints: target = the definitionLibrary entry; query = the member's words ("momentum", "volatility bands", "my trend"); kind = builtin | custom | null (both).

capabilities.name: definition.describe
capabilities.summary: Describe ONE indicator — its settings and their ranges, what it outputs, where it draws, and whether each output can drive an alert or a scan. Read-only.
capabilities.hints: target = the definitionLibrary entry; defId = its id (from a search or a chart's indicators list), or its exact name.

capabilities.name: definition.duplicate
capabilities.summary: Save a COPY of an indicator as one of the member's own indicators (the legend's "Create custom copy") — a built-in becomes an editable formula, one of theirs is forked. Shown first; Undo deletes the copy (while no chart draws it).
capabilities.hints: target = the definitionLibrary entry; defId = the indicator's id (or its exact name). To put an indicator on a chart twice use indicatorCopy.duplicate instead.

capabilities.name: definition.delete
capabilities.summary: Delete one of the member's OWN saved indicators (built-ins cannot be deleted). Always shown first, naming every chart still drawing it (they stop drawing it). Undo restores it under the same id, so those charts draw it again.
capabilities.hints: target = the definitionLibrary entry; defId = the indicator's id from yourIndicators or a chart's indicators list (or its exact name). If more than one of theirs could be meant, ask — never pick by similarity.

capabilities.name: agent.capabilities
capabilities.summary: Answer what UCT Agent can and cannot do (now, partly, not yet, planned) about a topic — from UCT's own capability list, never from memory.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the agent entry. Use ONLY for a question ABOUT abilities ("can you draw trendlines?", "what can you do with layouts?", "can you backtest?"). A polite request to DO something you can do ("can you switch this to weekly?") is a command: plan it, do not use this. topic: overview for "what can you do?"; other when no topic fits.

capabilities.name: agent.undo
capabilities.summary: Undo YOUR OWN most recent change(s) in this conversation — exactly what the Undo on that change’s receipt does. UCT refuses it itself when that change can’t be undone (changed since, another board, a protected layout, a permanent action).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the agent entry. scope: "last" = the newest change (undo that / undo the last change / revert it); "all" = every change of the previous request (undo all of that). about = what the member says the change was ("undo the timeframe change" → timeframe), else null. In a request that makes a change AND undoes it ("switch to weekly, then undo that"), put the change first and agent.undo LAST. Never tell the member you cannot undo, or to use another Undo: plan this, and UCT reports what it actually undid.

capabilities.name: guide.explain
capabilities.summary: Explain what a UCT term, indicator or feature IS (“what does ADR mean?”, “explain RSI”, “the difference between an indicator and a condition”), from UCT's own catalog. Changes nothing.
capabilities.hints: target = the guide entry. topic = the member's words for what to explain (an indicator, a UCT term or feature). Prefer it for UCT's own indicators and features — its text is UCT's catalog. Use ONLY for "what is / what does / explain / difference" questions; a request to change something is a command — plan it.

capabilities.name: guide.show
capabilities.summary: SHOW the member where a control is (on Charts, the Screener, Breadth, the Calendar or the Journal): highlight the real control on their screen with a short step-by-step card (Next / Back / Exit). Changes nothing — use it for "where do I…", "show me how to…", "how do I…" questions, never to do the thing.
capabilities.hints: target = the guide entry. feature = the walkthrough that teaches it: an id from the enum, each named for what it teaches (indicators, indicatorColor, drawing, multiChart, widgetResize, layoutSave, alertPrice, chartSetting…), and control for any other named control (a widget's button, a list's or a drawing's menu row: detail = the member's words); 7 ids belong to other pages and work only there. detail = the member's own words for which one ("the RSI", "a rectangle", "2x2") or for the chart they named ("the NVDA chart", "the left chart"), when they named one. A request to DO it ("change my chart to weekly") is a command, not this.

capabilities.name: calendar.day
capabilities.summary: List the earnings reports on ONE day (tickers by session: before the open / after the close), or the whole week when no day is given — from the week the Calendar page has loaded. Use it for "what reports on Thursday?", "who reports today?", "what's on this week?".
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the calendar entry; date = YYYY-MM-DD, or null for every day of the week on the page. Tickers only — no estimates.

capabilities.name: periodSort.run
capabilities.summary: Tools → Period Sort: rank US common stocks (or themes, sectors, industries) by their % change between a start and an end date, in a floating results panel — the popover's own Sort. Replay mode hides bars after the end date on every chart; Mark start draws the start date. A view: not saved; Undo closes it.
capabilities.hints: start / end = YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words ("oct 1"); end null = today. group = stocks | theme | sector | industry ("rank sectors since …" = sector). replay = true only when asked to hide bars after the end ("as of the end date"); false otherwise — exactly as the popover, Sort without Replay mode also turns an active replay off. markStart = off | line (gold line at the start) | candle (gold start candle). Never changes the charts' timeframe.

capabilities.name: periodSort.dock
capabilities.summary: Dock the open Period Sort results panel onto the board as a Period Sort widget (the panel's own Dock button), so it is kept with the layout. Undo takes it off the board and brings the panel back.
capabilities.hints: Only when a Period Sort panel is open (the context says which range). "Keep / pin / dock that ranking" = this. Adding it as a tab of another widget is not offered.

capabilities.name: multiChart.set
capabilities.summary: Change the Multi Chart GRID as a whole, as its Multi Charts menu does: open it at a shape (layout rows × columns) or exit to the Charts board, crosshair / time-range sync, Groups mode, load / step / refresh a group, open / save / delete a saved grid, open Shared Chart Settings, restore a maximized grid. Undo restores the grid exactly.
capabilities.hints: target = the multiChart ref. rows/cols only with op layout (both null = open Multi Chart as it was); on only with the sync / groupsMode ops; name = the group (pickGroup) or saved grid (applySaved / saveGrid / deleteSaved) as the member said it; direction only with stepGroup. ONE chart’s ticker / timeframe / style is a chart.* action on that cell, not this. Maximizing one cell or resetting one cell to the member’s own chart is multiChart.cell.

capabilities.name: multiChart.cell
capabilities.summary: ONE Multi Chart cell’s own buttons: maximize it so it covers the whole grid, or “Reset to my chart” (the cell drops its own chart settings and draws the member’s chart settings again; its ticker, timeframe and Style stay). Undo puts it back.
capabilities.hints: target = that cell’s ref from charts (the chart the member named or clicked). To un-maximize use multiChart.set op restoreGrid.
